# our_file: ../core/householder_qr.mojo
upstream_file: raft cpp/include/raft/linalg/detail/rsvd.cuh qrGetQ (:198) / cuSOLVER geqrf; and arima/impl/linalg/batched/least_squares.mojo (DEVIATION 678)
notes: TALL-SKINNY HOUSEHOLDER QR, ROW MAJOR, BLOCK PARALLEL, TSQR. There is no upstream arithmetic: cuSOLVER geqrf is closed and MAX ships qr_factorization with no bitwise contract, so the routine is written. WHAT IT REUSES rather than re-decides: the THREE SCALAR CHOICES arima's gated QR wrote down (DEVIATION 586) -- the reflector sign s = -sign(a_jj), u1 = a_jj - r_jj, tau = (-s*u1)/normx -- lifted here as qr_reflector_r / _u1 / _tau and living in exactly one place in the tree. WHAT IT DOES NOT REUSE, and why that is not a defect in either file: arima's LOOP is one thread per series, serial ascending, n <= 17, and this shape is one matrix at the shipped n_samples, so the fold is a pinned_block_sum halving tree (DEVIATION 587, not bitwise equal to arima's and not meant to be, bitwise equal across vendors) and the geometry is TSQR over a slice count that is a pure function of (n_rows, n_cols) (DEVIATION 589). NO RANK TEST (DEVIATION 588): this file never back substitutes, so a zero column norm is a zero singular value and H_j = I, which is what LAPACK's geqrf does and what lets svd_solver='full' accept a constant feature. The reflector's division is identical_div here and a bare `/` in arima's copy; the pairing patch for that is in the 2026-09-01 lane report and is NOT applied. Q IS NOT FORMED: orgqr is the piece TruncatedSVD(algorithm='randomized') still waits on

# our_file: impl/linalg/detail/svd_full.mojo
upstream_file: sklearn decomposition/_pca.py::_fit_full (:539-540 -> scipy.linalg.svd on the centered X); cuml cpp/src/pca/pca.cuh::pcaFit for the five outputs and their definitions
notes: R-SVD, DEVIATIONS 590/591/593. scikit-learn's 'full' is a dense SVD of X_c and cuML has no such arm at all (pca.pyx:394-395 maps both 'auto' and 'full' to COV_EIG_DQ), so the ALGORITHM is scikit-learn's and the OUTPUT DEFINITIONS are cuML's, which is why this row cites two upstreams. Route: column means and centering through the SAME two kernels the covariance arm calls, then core/householder_qr.mojo::qr_factor, then a ONE-SIDED cyclic Jacobi SVD of the n_cols x n_cols R (DEVIATION 590), then the shared sign_flip_kernel and order_truncate_spectrum. The one-sided Jacobi is not the shipped two-sided one and must not be: feeding R^T R to the eigensolver would put back the condition squaring the QR just removed. Its rotation is NOT a second copy -- jacobi_rotation_cs and _rot_sub/_rot_add are imported from jacobi_eigh_device.mojo. Its convergence test is relative and per pair, |apq| > tol*sqrt(app)*sqrt(aqq), written as two roots because app*aqq overflows Float32 on plausible data; its exit is a ROTATION COUNT, which is a machine-voted quantity of exactly the shape DEVIATION BLOCK 3 warns about, so every input to it is pinned. Non-convergence is REFUSED, not returned, following eigDC rather than eigJacobi. DEVIATION 593: n_samples < n_features is refused by name (the wide route is an LQ of the transpose, unwritten)

# our_file: impl/linalg/detail/pca.mojo::order_truncate_spectrum
notes: DEVIATION 591, and it is a MOVE not a rewrite: every line stood inside eig_and_truncate and is unchanged except that the eigenvalues arrive as a `diag` list instead of being read off the diagonal of the matrix the eigensolver left. Split out because the R-SVD arm reaches a spectrum without ever forming a covariance and so has no such matrix. THREE callers now share one definition of the descending order, the selection sort's tie behaviour, the ratio denominator, the sign convention's precondition and truncCompExpVars' two-part noise guard; the R-SVD arm hands it S^2/(n_rows-1) and the same singular_scale, so sqrt(lam*scale) returns S and the arms report the same five quantities by the same rules
